# @apexdevtools/apex-log-parser

> Turn a Salesforce Apex debug log into a typed event tree — execution timings, governor limits, SOQL/DML counts. Zero dependencies, ESM-only.

This library takes raw Salesforce Apex debug log text and produces a typed tree of parsed events. It has a dedicated class for 171 event types and a bundled database of 299 documented events. It computes execution timing (self and total duration in nanoseconds), tracks governor limits with per-namespace snapshots, and counts SOQL/DML/SOSL rows aggregated up the call tree.

## Quick Start

```typescript
import { parse } from '@apexdevtools/apex-log-parser';

const log = parse(debugLogText);

for (const event of log.children) {
  console.log(event.type, event.text, event.duration.total);
}
```

## Key APIs

The package has two entry points. The root exports runtime values only — the parser and the event
classes. Every type, and the const companions that go with them, come from
`@apexdevtools/apex-log-parser/types`.

```typescript
import { parse, MethodEntryLine } from '@apexdevtools/apex-log-parser';
import { LOG_LEVEL, type GovernorLimits } from '@apexdevtools/apex-log-parser/types';
```

- `parse(logData: string): ApexLog` — the usual entry point. There is no state to reset between calls
- `ApexLogParser` — the parser class. Public because every event constructor takes one, so code that builds events needs it
- `ApexLog` — the root node. A `LogEvent` plus `governorLimits`, `namespaces`, `debugLevels`, `logIssues`, `parsingErrors`, `exceptions`, `eventsById`, `startTime`, `size`, `truncation`, `truncatedEvents`
- `LogEvent` — base class for all events with `type`, `text`, `timestamp`, `exitStamp`, `duration`, `children`, `parent`, `namespace`, `lineNumber`, `eventIndex`, `category`, `debugCategory`, `debugLevel`, `cpuType`, and `SelfTotal` counters (`soqlCount`, `soqlRowCount`, `dmlCount`, `dmlRowCount`, `soslCount`, `soslRowCount`, `thrownCount`, `heapAllocated`, `heapGross`)
- Exported event subclasses, for `instanceof` narrowing: `ApexLog`, `CodeUnitStartedLine`, `DMLBeginLine`, `ExecutionStartedLine`, `HeapAllocateLine`, `LimitUsageLine`, `LogEvent`, `MethodEntryLine`, `SOQLExecuteBeginLine`, `SOQLExecuteExplainLine`, `SOSLExecuteBeginLine`. For any other event type compare `event.type` as a string — it is typed as `LogEventType`
- `DebugLevel` class — `{ logCategory, logLevel }`
- From `/types`, constants: `ALL_LOG_CATEGORIES`, `DEBUG_CATEGORY`, `LOG_CATEGORY`, `LOG_LEVEL`
- From `/types`, types: `CPUType`, `DebugCategory`, `GovernorLimits`, `GovernorSnapshot`, `IssueType`, `LimitMetricKey`, `LimitObservation`, `Limits`, `LineNumber`, `LogCategory`, `LogEventType`, `LogIssue`, `LogLevel`, `RunningTotalObservation`, `SelfTotal`, `Truncation`, `TruncationRegion`

## Governor Limits

```typescript
import { parse } from '@apexdevtools/apex-log-parser';

const log = parse(debugLogText);
log.governorLimits.cpuTime;       // { used, limit }
log.governorLimits.soqlQueries;   // { used, limit }
log.governorLimits.dmlStatements; // { used, limit }
log.governorLimits.byNamespace;   // Map<string, Limits>
log.governorLimits.snapshots;     // GovernorSnapshot[]
```

The log must contain a `CUMULATIVE_LIMIT_USAGE` block, which needs `APEX_PROFILING` at `FINE` or above. Without it every metric stays at `{ used: 0, limit: 0 }`.

## Event Database

A bundled JSON database of 299 Salesforce debug log event types is available:

```typescript
import events from '@apexdevtools/apex-log-parser/data/events.json' with { type: 'json' };
```
